newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN refugee agency evacuates some staff from Zaire.
newsitem.headline: UN refugee agency evacuates some staff from Zaire.

text.p: The United Nations refugee agency said on Friday that it had evacuated 10 of its 19 international staff from Uvira, Zaire in recent days due to harrassment, threats and the generally worsening security situation there.
But the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) said essential expatriate staff had stayed behind to run its aid programme for 219,466 Burundi and Rwandan refugees living in 13 camps in the area.
"We remain extremely concerned about the security situation in the Great Lakes region, especially in eastern Zaire," UNHCR spokesman Ron Redmond told a news briefing.

UNHCR staff in Uvira, located in Zaire's South Kivu region, attend daily meetings to assess the security situation with other expatriates working for non-governmental organisations, according to Redmond.

Six UNHCR expatriate staff flew out of Uvira to Nairobi on Wednesday, followed by another four on Friday, according to the Geneva-based agency. Six international staff of non-governmental organisations flew out on the same plane on Friday.
UNHCR spokesman Fernando del Mundo told Reuters: "Essential staff remain.
"There have been a lot of incidents involving expatriate staff -- harassment, cars being taken at gunpoint in Uvira," he added. "There have been threats against UNHCR staff. Staff have been harassed.
At the height of the influx of Rwandan refugees fleeing genocide in 1994, UNHCR employed some 70 expatriates in Uvira.
